analysis:
The PR adds a `publish_revision_only` boolean to `.github/workflows/register-model.yml` (head lines 9-13).

- When the flag is set, the full registration payload step is skipped (head line 94).
- A minimal payload of `{version, hugging_face_artifact}` is built instead (head lines 175-183).
- That payload is POSTed to `/v1/admin/models/<urlquoted model_id>/publish-revision` (head lines 193-195), with the same `MODEL_REGISTRY_PUBLISHING_KEY` bearer token.
- All untrusted inputs flow through env vars, not inline `${{ }}` in the shell. `MODEL_ID` is percent-encoded with `safe=""` via Python, so there is no path traversal or script injection.
- The `coordinator_url` input, which receives the bearer key, is pre-existing behavior and not new.
- The publish-revision endpoint semantics are backend-owned and out of the provider threat-model scope. This includes promotion without the separate `promote` flag and validation of `hugging_face_artifact` revision pins. Model-weight integrity (A-004, T-012, T-027) still depends on platform-side validation; this workflow adds no client-side checks.
- Required inputs (`display_name`, prices, etc.) remain mandatory even in revision-only mode. This is a usability issue only.
- `changelog.d/model-publication-workflow.md` and the `docs/developer/test.md` additions (head lines 443-456) are documentation only. They reference `scripts/test_model_registry_workflow.py`, `scripts/test_publish_model_revision.py` and `docs/operations/model-revisions.md`, none of which were supplied. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.

No provider attestation, encryption, authorization or billing code paths changed. No findings.
